title: Andhra man storms school with chainsaw, attacks Class 10 girl he stalked
content: In Anantapur district, a male assailant attacked a tenth-grade student named Gopika with a saw. This violent incident occurred inside a Zilla Parishad high school, shocking students and staff members alike. Another student, Lakshmi, sustained injuries while trying to intervene and protect her classmate. Local police were promptly notified and initiated a search for the suspect. Authorities are conducting a thorough investigation to apprehend the perpetrator and ensure community safety.

title: Cargo ship stranded in Pakistan for months, sailor’s kin high & dry
content: Vedansh Mishra, a three-year-old, frequently asks about his father, Vineet, who is stranded in Karachi, Pakistan. Vineet has been unable to leave the cargo ship since April, with his family seeking help from politicians. Despite appeals to government officials, the family has yet to achieve a resolution in bringing him home. Communication with Vineet is limited due to poor network connectivity and ongoing ship conditions.

title: 'Not looking at him for white-ball cricket': Is Jadeja's ODI career over?
content: The 37-year-old was not included in India's squad for the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, with Axar Patel currently the team's first-choice left-arm finger spinner.

title: Centre scraps Rs 2.5/litre petrol export duty, hikes diesel levy to Rs 11.5
content: The Centre took significant steps on October 31 by eliminating the Rs 2.5 per litre duty on petrol exports. In contrast, the excise duties for high-speed diesel and aviation turbine fuel were ramped up; diesel duties increased from Rs 8.5 to Rs 11.5 per litre, and ATF duties from Rs 10.5 to Rs 11.

title: Amazon has a question for its engineering teams that are slow to adopt AI
content: Amazon has asked engineering leaders to focus on teams slowest to adopt AI and find out why, as part of an updated role guideline for software development engineers. The internal memo also calls AI usage metrics like token counts deeply flawed, says teams not adopting AI are falling behind, and tells its engineers it is fine if current AI tools do not help their work.

title: After surviving 85% burns at 21, man helps feed hundreds of US students
content: Joey Brown endured a life-changing gas explosion that led to severe burns and extensive surgeries. He regained independence through employment with support from his community and vocational rehabilitation services. While working in a high school cafeteria, he developed meaningful relationships and has become an encouragement to others. Brown is now aiming to buy his own home and adopt a beagle named Snoopy.

title: Hundreds evacuated from Oleshky as Melania Trump brokers rare Russia-Ukraine ceasefire
content: Hundreds of residents were evacuated from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky during a humanitarian ceasefire. The evacuation allowed individuals to leave amidst dire conditions of starvation and exhaustion. Three planes carrying evacuees successfully landed at an airport in Belarus as part of a coordinated operation. Both Russian and Ukrainian authorities confirmed the operation was conducted without any incidents.

title: Connecticut's eelgrass shrank 90%; volunteers now plant seeds on clams
content: In a creative effort to restore the eelgrass meadows of Long Island Sound, volunteers in Connecticut have adopted an innovative technique. By attaching eelgrass seeds to clam shells, they facilitate the seeds' ability to embed into the seabed, leading to improved growth rates. Although early results show higher eelgrass coverage, there are ongoing concerns about long-term resilience. This initiative is a prime example of community-driven, nature-based environmental restoration strategies.

title: Ancient Spanish copper mine may be linked to 11 Scandinavian bronze objects
content: Excavations at the Las Minillas site in Spain have unveiled substantial copper mining activities dating back to the Late Bronze Age. Investigations revealed a chemical link between the site and bronze artifacts discovered in Scandinavia. Researchers noted extensive mining operations and identified numerous nearby mining locations, indicating that southern Iberia was crucial for copper supply in Europe during this period.

title: Canada sets this condition for international students looking to work there
content: Canada's immigration authority emphasizes that international students may work only if their study permits allow it. Students can work off campus for a maximum of 24 hours per week during study sessions. Violating these work conditions can lead to serious repercussions, including loss of student status. Furthermore, unauthorized work may result in a permanent record of fraud with IRCC and a five-year return ban.

title: Psychology says a collecting mindset can make shopping more enjoyable
content: People often find joy in viewing purchases as additions to collections rather than isolated items. This perspective shifts focus towards the experience of searching and acquiring meaningful objects. Retailers utilize collecting strategies to encourage consumers to build sets and return for more items. Research indicates that this mindset can influence spending and price evaluations, impacting consumer behavior. Overall, the process of collecting infuses purchases with emotional resonance beyond mere functionality.

title: From slum walls to classrooms: Mumbai artist wins $1 million Global Teacher Prize
content: Indian artist and educator Rouble Nagi has won the $1 million GEMS Education Global Teacher Prize 2026 for transforming neglected walls into interactive learning spaces for children in underserved communities. Through her Rouble Nagi Art Foundation, she has established over 800 learning centres across more than 100 communities, helping over one million children access formal education. Nagi plans to use the prize money to establish a Skilling Institute offering free vocational and digital literacy training.

title: Nifty50 faces worst year in a decade: Will November help Dalal Street to bounce back?
content: October was a challenging month for Indian stocks, leading to a cautious perspective for November. The recent dip in the Nifty50 has sparked recovery hopes, even as elevated crude oil prices and AI sector trends may pose obstacles. Interestingly, foreign investors seem to be transitioning from a pessimistic to a more neutral position, influencing market behavior.

title: Lift crashes down at high speed in Mumbai suburban's 7-storey building; 8 injured
content: Eight individuals suffered injuries when a lift malfunctioned and fell in Dhananjay Avenue, Nalasopara. Residents reported that the lift dropped suddenly while occupants were traveling to the ground floor. Witnesses helped rescue those trapped inside the lift and transported them to a local hospital. Among the injured was advocate Satish Bhondve, along with his guests who were in the lift.

title: US rolls out Stinger missiles to shield Trump's Florida estate from drone threats
content: To bolster security around Mar-a-Lago estate, the United States has installed Avenger air defense systems. These advanced systems address potential airborne threats like drones and low-flying aircraft, responding to a heightened need highlighted by the US Secret Service. Equipped with Stinger missiles, the Avenger system effectively counters various aerial dangers, illustrating the growing concerns related to unmanned aerial vehicles in contemporary security threats.

title: California barber built $19m fortune; court revives elder abuse claims
content: Maurice Voce, a successful barber whose financial savvy amassed significant wealth, tragically deteriorated in health prior to his passing. Following his death, concerns arose about the effectiveness of his financial adviser's management amid Voce's cognitive difficulties. His family has since initiated a lawsuit against Morgan Stanley and adviser John Privitelli, alleging financial elder abuse.

title: ‘Send him home’: Ex-cricketer's blunt message to Gambhir over Sooryavanshi
content: Aakash Chopra has voiced his concerns regarding India’s choice to omit Vaibhav Sooryavanshi from the lineup for the fourth T20I. He stressed the importance of clear communication about Sooryavanshi's position and future with the team. Although he had previously shown strong performance, Sooryavanshi was dropped upon Ishan Kishan’s return. Chopra suggests that if Sooryavanshi is not a priority, he should focus on gaining more experience in domestic cricket.

title: Bengaluru man says family spends up to Rs 80,000 monthly on home-cooked food
content: A four-person family in Bengaluru claims their monthly grocery bills range between Rs 60,000 to Rs 80,000, sparking discussions across social media platforms regarding average grocery costs. Various users chimed in, sharing their own budgeting experiences, which showcased stark contrasts in spending behaviors. The discourse emphasizes that food expenditure can be highly individualized, influenced by personal preferences and lifestyle choices.

title: Japan's 'phone booth to the dead' lets people talk to lost loved ones
content: In the heart of Otsuchi, Japan, the Wind Phone stands as a poignant tribute to those who have lost loved ones. Established by Itaru Sasaki after the loss of his cousin, this unique telephone booth offers a space to share unspoken thoughts. Following the devastation of the 2011 tsunami, it has become a refuge for many grieving souls, fostering emotional connections and inspiring similar creations worldwide.

title: 13-year-old Goan girl turns backyard moringa into powder business
content: During her summer break, Grace de Souza, a talented teenager from Goa, tapped into her entrepreneurial spirit by producing moringa powder from the leaves of her family's two moringa trees. Her efforts have proven fruitful, with earnings nearing Rs 3,000 from selling 20 packets. Inspired by this success, Grace plans to sustain her small business even when school resumes, embracing the lessons of hard work and responsibility.

title: German, Slovak nationals die of electrocution in Bengaluru 5-star hotel pool
content: On Friday evening, two foreign nationals from Germany and Slovakia died from suspected electrocution in a hotel swimming pool. A US national and an Indian pool attendant were injured while trying to rescue them. Both the injured individuals were taken to Manipal Hospital for treatment, and they are currently reported to be out of danger. Police have initiated an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.

title: No more unknown calls! Govt mandates displaying names - here's what changes from Nov 1
content: From November 1, telecom operators will implement Calling Name Presentation, changing how incoming calls are displayed. This new feature will show caller names for both saved and unsaved numbers, depending on subscriber details. International calls will be labeled as 'International Call' regardless of the user's saved contacts. Businesses and users with bulk connections can register preferred names subject to verification requirements.

title: 'Sher ki tarah jhapatta': How Manisha overturned 0-6 deficit to win gold at Worlds
content: Manisha Bhanwala made history as the first Indian woman to win gold at the Wrestling World Championships, overcoming a 0-6 deficit to triumph. After the win, she showcased a t-shirt with a photo of her late father, who introduced her to the sport. With her sights now set on the 57kg Olympic category for LA 2028, Manisha’s experience and resilience will be crucial for future success.

title: Pennsylvania couple's six-year fight revives truck stop drive-through plan
content: After almost six years of legal back-and-forth, a Pennsylvania convenience store finally received the go-ahead for a drive-through window. Jyotsna and Anil Jivani's 2020 proposal faced initial denial from township officials. However, in a significant ruling from the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court in October 2026, judges overturned the lower court's verdict, affirming that the drive-through serves as a natural extension of their business, paving the way for construction approval.

title: Meet Joan Ginther, who won $20m across four lottery jackpots
content: Joan Ginther stands out in lottery history, having triumphantly won the Texas Lottery four times in 17 years, accumulating an astounding $20.4 million in total. This unprecedented success has sparked intrigue, particularly regarding her statistical background. Investigators have examined whether her victories stemmed from calculated strategies or perhaps some insider knowledge. The question remains: Is her extraordinary luck a result of clever choices or merely chance?

title: IIM Calcutta alumna on how life changed after switching from McKinsey to Google
content: Jahnvi Singh's career shift from McKinsey to Google has significantly enhanced her work-life balance and transformed her daily schedule. She now focuses on a single business, which deepens her industry expertise while reducing the need for frequent domestic travel. This change opens opportunities for international trips, and she enjoys improved workplace perks at Google. Most notably, Jahnvi has rediscovered time for fitness and socializing, which had previously been difficult.

title: US midterm elections: What a Democratic win could mean for India's trade
content: The midterm elections in the United States are approaching, and results may affect trade relations with India. A Democratic win could lead to increased scrutiny of current trade policies, including tariffs and government spending. However, significant policy changes are not expected immediately following the elections. The investment landscape for artificial intelligence and data centres is unlikely to face substantial shifts.

title: 'Won't move forward without public': Arunachal CM amid protests over Siang project
content: Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu has assured residents that the proposed 11,200-MW Siang hydropower project will not be imposed on them, saying a decision will be taken only after its feasibility report is completed. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China's mega dam upstream, faces opposition from indigenous Adi communities over displacement, submergence of villages and environmental concerns.

title: 'Real danger, real need': Why Zelenskyy wants Patriot missiles before winter
content: Ukraine is urgently requesting Patriot air defence interceptors to bolster its defense against increased Russian strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed concerns over potential delays in receiving these crucial missiles. The impending winter raises fears of vulnerable civilians if critical infrastructure is damaged. European countries face challenges in balancing support for Ukraine with their own defense needs.

title: Arizona parents turn donated van into charity fighting inherited blindness
content: After their son Luke was diagnosed with Bardet-Biedl syndrome, an Arizona couple established A Race Against Blindness. The charity has since raised over $6.1 million for research into inherited retinal diseases. They also organized a sweepstakes featuring a custom adventure van, significantly increasing awareness. Their contributions support groundbreaking gene therapy aimed at BBS1, and funding has expanded to multiple inherited retinal condition studies.

title: '20 villas in Udaipur, 8 in Alwar': Why IAS officer, IPS wife face corruption probe
content: Senior IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal faces a preliminary inquiry by the Anti-Corruption Bureau. He has been accused of misusing his official position to benefit Goyal Fashions Private Limited. The inquiry includes alleged irregularities in the purchase of villas by Agrawal and his family members. Agrawal reportedly secured financial benefits for the company while he was in charge of industries.

title: Sanjay Gupta Dies: Filmmaker behind Kaante and Shootout at Wadala dies at 57
content: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has reportedly passed away, with Kamaal Khan paying tribute on X. Debuting with ‘Aatish: Feel the Fire’ in 1994, Gupta became known for crime dramas and stylised action, including ‘Kaante’, ‘Shootout at Wadala’, ‘Kaabil’ and ‘Mumbai Saga’. The cause of death hasn’t been disclosed.

title: Dhruv Jurel's unbeaten 99 rescues India A after dramatic collapse against NZ A
content: Dhruv Jurel played a crucial role for India A by scoring an unbeaten 99 in tough conditions. After losing three wickets in quick succession, India A struggled at 160 for 6 during the match. Jurel built partnerships including a vital 62-run stand with Manav Suthar, who contributed 22 runs. He remained unbeaten as India A fought back to reach a competitive total by day's end.

title: Man shares strict chore list his dad made him follow from age 8
content: A chore list shared by a user highlights parenting methods for young children and their responsibilities. The reactions indicate divided opinions on how much structure is beneficial for children. Some parents recall gaining important life skills from similar routines while others express regret about a lack of structure. Research connects children performing chores with improved competence and relationships during later school years.

title: Meet Ayaan Wadhwa, 17: Mumbai teen helps 750 domestic workers get govt benefits
content: Ayaan Wadhwa was inspired to help domestic workers in Mumbai after a personal incident involving financial insecurity. He organized workshops to educate workers about government welfare schemes and assist them in registering for benefits. His efforts have benefitted more than 750 unorganised-sector workers, addressing their lack of awareness. Additionally, he is developing an AI-powered WhatsApp chatbot to simplify contract creation for domestic workers.

title: 'Punjabion ko naa sikhaao...': Diljit Dosanjh's pointed message amid CJP row

Dosanjh defended his film on human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, which was ridiculed by critics. Testimony from Donna Rhorer revealed disturbing insights about operational practices. Federal investigations uncovered multiple alarming incidents, leading to possible decertification for the Network for Hope, as the family demands accountability.
